commitResults.messageTitle: Say when a folder has the name of the file to write
commitResults.messageBody:
Exporting a record when a folder has the name of its file, e.g.,
data/exports/S0000001A.txt, gave only the file system's own reason,
"Is a directory", which other systems word differently, or report as
a missing permission on Windows.

Let's check for such a folder before writing, in
FileUtil#writeThroughTemporaryFile, and give a reason that names the
problem and how to fix it. No temporary file is then made at all.

Fixes #476

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the file that is in place of the backup folder
commitResults.messageBody:
restore FILENAME said that no backup was found in data/backups when
data/backups, or the data folder above it, was a file. restore alone
already says that a file is in the way, as backup cannot make the
folder while that file is there.

Let's name that file in RestoreCommand#describeMissingBackup too,
through FileUtil#findFileInPlaceOfFolder, so that both forms of
restore give the same advice.

Fixes #475

commitResults.messageTitle: Say that a backup name has a character Windows does not allow
commitResults.messageBody:
On Windows, restore "my backup.json", with quotes, said "Give only
the name of a backup file in data/backups, not a path", although the
name has no folder in it. Windows does not allow quotes, and also <,
>, |, ? and *, in file names, so Paths#get rejects such a name, and
the parser took that to mean a path.

Let's check what the operating system allows separately, and say
that the name has a character that file names cannot have, and to
type it without quotes. macOS and Linux still take quotes as part of
the name, as the UG says.

Fixes #474

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the restore and export messages for files in the way
commitResults.messageBody:
restore FILENAME now also names a file that is in place of the backup
folder, or of the data folder, and export gives its own reason when a
folder has the name of the record file.

Let's say so in the restore and export sections of the UG, in the DG
paragraph on how restore reports a missing backup, in the note of the
restore activity diagram, and in the manual test for a file named
data.

Refs #475, #476

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the folder that is in place of the file to write
commitResults.messageBody:
The reason given for a folder with the name of the file to write said
"there is a folder with that name", but a failed save of the data file
shows the reason without the file's path, so "that name" had nothing
to refer to.

Let's name the folder in the reason, as is done for a file in place
of a folder.

Refs #476

commitResults.messageTitle: Point the Command Summary link at the command summary
commitResults.messageBody:
The site map's Command Summary link opened the FAQ, as it pointed at
UserGuide.html#faq, the same target as the FAQ link above it.

Let's point it at UserGuide.html#command-summary.

Fixes #468

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the intended users at the start of the User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG introduction described a generic patient-record app, so a
first-time reader did not learn whom MediConnect is for, although the
DG's product scope says so.

Let's add two sentences, matching the DG's target user profile and
value proposition: the main and secondary users, and that the app
keeps each patient's care information in one place.

Fixes #461

commitResults.messageTitle: Say that indices must come before prefixed parameters
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG said that parameters can be in any order. That holds for
parameters with a prefix, but INDEX and MED_INDEX must come first,
in the order shown, e.g., editmed t/08:00 1 2 is rejected.

Let's state both rules, with an example of each.

Fixes #460

commitResults.messageTitle: Define the result box and the status message
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG used "result box" once without introducing it, and the DG's
manual tests call the same text the "status message", which could be
taken for the status bar. The UG also called the detail panel the
"details panel" and the "view panel" in one place each.

Let's name the result box in the Quick start, define the status
message once at the start of the manual-testing appendix, and use
"detail panel" throughout.

Fixes #488

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the screenshot, diagrams and photos in alt text
commitResults.messageBody:
The main screenshot's alternative text was only "Ui", nine DG
diagrams had none, and neither had the AboutUs photos or the MarkBind
logo in the footer.

Let's describe what each screenshot and diagram shows, name each
member in their photo's alt text, and mark the footer logo, which
the word MarkBind follows, as decorative.

Fixes #480

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a draft Effort appendix to the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
Effort raters in the PE read the DG appendix named Effort, if any,
when comparing the team's work with AB3, and the DG has none yet.

Let's add a short appendix: the size of MediConnect compared with
AB3, measured from the repository, why the patient model is harder
than AB3's single entity, the main challenges, and the reuse. Each
claim was checked against the code. Team members can add to the
parts about their own features.

Refs #448

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover the new restore messages in UC9 and the export steps
commitResults.messageBody:
UC9 had no extension for a name with a character that the operating
system does not allow, or for restore FILENAME when data/backups
cannot be read or is a file, which restore now reports. The export
steps in the DG named only the read-only case that
FileUtil#writeThroughTemporaryFile reports.

Let's add UC9 extensions 3d and 3e, and say in the export steps that
a folder with the file's name is reported too.

Refs #474, #475, #476

commitResults.messageTitle: Say that Tab moves the focus to the result box
commitResults.messageBody:
The view manual test said that Tab moves the focus between the
command box and the status message. The appendix now defines the
status message as the message shown in the result box, and it is the
result box that takes the focus.

Refs #488

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain once how characters are counted in the UG
commitResults.messageBody:
Only the contact section said that an emoji or a separately typed
accent can count as more than one character, although every length
limit counts characters the same way, and fields differ in whether
they combine a separately typed accent with its letter.

Let's add a short subsection under Field formats, worded from tests
on the app: basic emoji count as one, emoji made from several symbols
as more, and a separately typed accent as two, except in medications,
allergens and care instructions, which are saved with the accent
combined. The contact section links to it instead of repeating it.

Fixes #466
Refs #492

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that a failed final replacement deletes the temporary file
commitResults.messageBody:
FileUtil#writeThroughTemporaryFile deletes its temporary file if the
final replacement of the file fails. A test made that replacement fail
with a folder at the file's path, but #493 now rejects such a folder
before writing, so no test would cover that cleanup any more.

Let's add a test whose writer makes a folder that is not empty at the
file's path while the content is written, after the early check, so
that the replacement itself fails, and check that only the folder is
left.

Suggested by @JellehBelleh in the review of #493.
Explain once how characters are counted in the UG
Give clear messages when a name, folder or file is in the way of restore or export
Correct clear test message
Correct reserved slash text examples

commitResults.messageTitle: Say in the UG that delete makes no backup
commitResults.messageBody:
The delete section did not say that delete makes no backup and
cannot be undone, although clear and restore both back up the data
first. A user could expect the same and lose the patient for good.

Say so where users read about delete, as Prof Damith asked for
limitations, and point to archive, and to backup before deleting,
with what restore then replaces.

Fixes #539

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Romy's suggestions to the DG Effort appendix
commitResults.messageBody:
Romy suggested, in #495, points for the Challenges part covering the
medication, due and find features.

Add a bullet on medications with daily times, and say how due
combines the doses of all patients and keeps its mark apart from
descriptions. Add one-digit hours, curly apostrophes and regression
tests to the real-world text bullet, and the loading of v1.3 data
files to the data safety bullet.

Leave out the find changes of #541 until it merges, as suggested.
Let editmed accept the addcare slash words
Document known limits
Let find split keywords at commas and ignore accents

Add Romy's suggestions to the DG Effort appendix

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix three small docs inaccuracies in UG and DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG did not say how to restore a backup whose name ends in .JSON
in another letter case, which leaving out the extension does not
find on Linux. Say to type the full name as restore lists it.

In the DG, the copy story was marked unlikely to have although the
detail panel implements it, and the Effort table still gave the test
line count from before #541.

Fixes #549

commitResults.messageTitle: Let editmed accept the addcare slash words
commitResults.messageBody:
addcare keeps the standalone words s/o, d/o, c/o, a/l, a/p and w/o as
text in a medication description, but editmed rejects d/o, a/l, a/p
and w/o with "Unrecognized parameter".

As a result, a medication added with "w/o food" cannot be edited
without dropping that text, although both commands write the same
field.

Let's move the addcare list to CliSyntax as ALLOWED_SLASH_WORDS and
pass it to EditMedCommandParser as well.

One shared list keeps the two commands consistent, and only the two
parsers that write medication descriptions change. As in addcare, the
words must be written without punctuation attached.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the slash words that editmed allows
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG and DG list addcare, editcare, addappt and editappt as the
commands that allow w/o, and the editmed section names no standalone
slash words.

Now that editmed accepts them, a user reading the UG would still
write "without", and a tester could report the UG as wrong.

Let's add editmed to those lists, state the words in the editmed
section with an example, and add a DG manual test.

The wording matches the addcare section, so both commands read the
same way.

commitResults.messageTitle: Note editmed and find limits in the UG
commitResults.messageBody:
editmed reads a time typed without a space before t/ as part of the
description, find keeps a comma or semicolon as part of a keyword,
and find does not match a name whose accents are left out.

The UG does not mention any of these, so a user can lose a time
change or miss a patient without knowing why.

Let's add a note for each one where the user reads about that field,
with the workaround and the change planned for a future version.

Testers then see these as known, planned limits rather than bugs, and
users know how to avoid them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Note the due name limit and what due means
commitResults.messageBody:
due shows the NRIC only for names that are stored identically apart
from letter case, so two names that differ only in how an accent is
stored look the same. The UG also says due lists the times at which
medications "are taken", and a DG user story says it lets a caregiver
check for missed doses.

A caregiver could fail to tell two patients apart, or take the
(earlier today) mark as a record of a missed dose.

Let's state that limit with the due INDEX workaround, say that the
mark only means the time has passed, and reword the intro and the
user story so neither implies dose tracking.

The UG and DG then match what due does and what it does not do.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say which spaces duplicate checks ignore
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG and DG say duplicate care entries and medications are found
ignoring "whitespace differences". The checks ignore repeated and
special spaces only, so "Amlodipine 5 mg" is not a duplicate of
"Amlodipine 5mg". The data file section also leaves out equivalent
Unicode forms, which the loader does ignore.

A tester who follows the UG would report the second entry as a bug.

Let's say "repeated or special spaces" in addcare, editmed, editcare,
the data file section and the DG, with the 5 mg example in addcare
and editmed, and list equivalent Unicode forms wherever duplicates
are described.

The wording then matches the checks in the commands and the loader.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix the due line format and UC4 in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG due implementation gives only the HH:MM NAME: DESCRIPTION line
format, and UC4 extension 5c does not cover more than two indexes.

Both differ from the code and from the UG, so a developer reading the
DG gets an incomplete picture.

Let's describe the (NRIC) line format and how names are compared, and
copy the UC5 wording for 5c into UC4.

The DG then matches DueCommand and the editmed parser.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match the model and delete diagrams to code
commitResults.messageBody:
In the model class diagram, the 0..1 and 0..* labels at Patient
overlap and read as 0..10..*. The delete sequence diagram shows
deletePatient(1), but Model#deletePatient takes a Patient.

Both diagrams mislead a developer about the model.

Let's place each label beside its own arrow, and show DeleteCommand
getting the displayed list before it deletes the patient it found.
The note under the diagram no longer calls the Model interaction a
single step.

The diagrams then match ModelManager and DeleteCommand#execute.

commitResults.messageTitle: Note the unspecific time error in editmed
commitResults.messageBody:
When one of several t/ values is not a valid time, editmed returns
the general time format message without naming the value, so a time
such as "08:00," with a comma looks valid.

A user cannot tell which time to fix and may retype the whole
command.

Let's add a note next to the time rules with that example, the fix
to make, and the change planned for a future version.

The user then knows to check each t/ value and to separate times
with spaces only.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let find split keywords at commas
commitResults.messageBody:
find splits keywords at spaces only, so a comma or semicolon stays in
the keyword. "find alex, bernice" lists only Bernice Yu, and
"find alex;bernice" finds no one.

Typing a list with commas is a common habit, and the patient left out
is easy to miss.

Let's split keywords at commas and semicolons too, and report a
command that has only those characters as having no keyword.

Names cannot contain commas or semicolons, so no name stops matching.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let find ignore accent marks in names
commitResults.messageBody:
find matches an accented letter only when the keyword has the same
accent, so "find zoe" does not find Zoë Tan, although most keyboards
cannot easily type ë.

A caregiver searching as they type would think the patient is not in
MediConnect.

Let's remove accent marks (U+0300 to U+036F) from names and keywords
before comparing them, in the find predicate only.

Accented and plain spellings then both match, while letters such as
ø and ß, marks of other scripts, and the shared duplicate checks stay
as they are.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe input normalization in the DG parser text
commitResults.messageBody:
Since #441, AddressBookParser turns tabs, no-break spaces and other
horizontal whitespace into spaces before a command's parser runs. The
DG still says that arguments are unchanged and that a tab does not
start a free-text field.

A developer following the DG would expect a tab to stay inside a
field value and could misjudge where fields start.

Let's describe the steps in order: normalize the whitespace, split
off and lowercase the command word, then pass the rest to the parser,
and say that a tab before a supported prefix starts a field.

The DG then matches AddressBookParser#normalizeWhitespace and the
tokenizer's field boundary.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the real configuration in the guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The Configuration guide says the preferences file location and the
logging level are set in a config.json file. MediConnect has no such
file: the paths are constants in MainApp and the logging settings are
constants in LogsCenter.

A developer following the guide would look for a file the app never
reads.

Let's list what is fixed in the code and where, link the Logging
guide, and link the Configuration guide from the DG.

The guide then matches MainApp, BackupCommand and LogsCenter.

commitResults.messageTitle: Call the product MediConnect in the setup guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The setup guide links to "AddressBook's architecture", although the
link opens the MediConnect Developer Guide.

A new contributor could think the guide describes the sample app
rather than this project.

Let's name the link "MediConnect's architecture".

The setup guide then uses the product's own name throughout.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a setup path without IntelliJ
commitResults.messageBody:
The setup guide gives the JDK version, run and verification steps
only for IntelliJ users.

A contributor using another editor or the command line cannot tell
which JDK to use or how to run and check the project.

Let's state the JDK 25 requirement first and add Gradle steps to
check the JDK, run MediConnect and verify the setup.

The IntelliJ path stays as it is, and both paths enable assertions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Agree on CI setup for forks in two guides
commitResults.messageBody:
The setup guide says CI needs no setup, while the DevOps guide asks
fork owners to follow a Codecov guide.

A new contributor cannot tell whether a fork is fully set up after
forking.

Let's say in both guides that CI runs in a fork without setup and
that Codecov is optional, with a link from the setup guide to the
Code coverage section.

A fork run with no CODECOV_TOKEN still passed, so the text matches
what CI does.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the real StringUtilTest in the testing guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The testing guide gives seedu.address.commons.StringUtilTest as an
example of a unit test. The class is in seedu.address.commons.util.

A contributor who copies the name into a test runner cannot find
the class.

Let's give the full name of the existing class.

All three examples on the page then name classes that exist.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain how to run the checks that CI runs
commitResults.messageBody:
The testing guide gives only "gradlew clean test", but CI runs
"gradlew check coverage", under Xvfb on Linux, plus repository-wide
checks.

A local run can pass while CI fails, and GUI tests that skip without
a display can go unnoticed.

Let's add a section with the CI command, the coverage and test report
locations, the Xvfb command and a link to the repository-wide checks.

Developers can then reproduce a CI run before they push.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the local MarkBind build to the docs guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The Documentation guide links to a general MarkBind tutorial but
gives no commands for this repository, and one sentence is missing
"to".

A contributor cannot tell how to build or preview the website before
opening a pull request.

Let's give the npm commands from docs/package.json, what they need,
where the output goes, and how the version differs from CI's.

The commands were run on a clean copy and built the site with no
warnings.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the log file name and rotation
commitResults.messageBody:
The Logging guide says only that logs go to "a .log file".

A developer looking for the log cannot tell where it is, what it is
called or when it rotates.

Let's give the file name, its folder, the 5 MiB and five-file
rotation, and the LogsCenter constants that set them.

The guide then matches LogsCenter and the files that MediConnect
writes.

The docs folder still has AB3 template files that no page uses: two
add-remark diagrams, a legacy tracing diagram, three PNG copies of
diagrams that the DG embeds as .puml, two images, an orphaned Jekyll
Gemfile.lock and an unused img.png. The docs package is described as
"AB-3 docs".

They are copied into the website and suggest current design material
that does not exist.

Let's delete them and describe the package as MediConnect docs.

No file in the repository refers to them, and the website builds
with no broken links.

commitResults.messageTitle: Declare my AI use in the DG
Clarify which accent marks find ignores
commitResults.messageBody: Clarified handling of accent marks in keyword searches.

commitResults.messageTitle: Declare my ChatGPT use in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
My AI-use line in the Developer Guide names only Claude Code, but I
also used ChatGPT to audit the docs and prepare test checklists.

The course asks each member to declare the AI tools they used.

Let's add ChatGPT to my line, in the same format as the other lines.

The declaration then names every tool I used.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use runnable commands in the undo walkthrough
commitResults.messageBody:
The proposed undo/redo walkthrough starts with a first launch, which
loads four sample patients, and then runs `delete 5`. Its second
state diagram is titled `editmed 1 1`, a command that changes nothing
and is rejected, although Step 3 runs `editmed 1 1 med/Aspirin 75mg`.

A reader who tries the steps on the sample data gets errors, and the
diagrams do not match the text.

Let's delete the 4th patient in Step 2 and in its diagram, and give
the second diagram the full editmed command of Step 3.

Every step of the walkthrough then works on the sample data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the find changes to the Effort appendix
commitResults.messageBody:
The Real-world text bullet of the Effort appendix lists the forms of
input that MediConnect accepts, but not the find changes of #541:
keywords split at commas and semicolons, and common accent marks are
ignored.

These changes are part of the work on real-world text, and #546 asks
for them to be added once #541 and #545 are in.

Let's add one sentence on them to the bullet, worded as in the User
Guide.

The appendix then covers all the merged handling of real-world text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the Patient diagram at a readable size
commitResults.messageBody:
The Patient class diagram is about 900px wide but is shown at 450px, so its attributes and multiplicities are hard to read.

Let's drop the fixed width so it renders at its natural size; the page already scales images down on narrow screens.

Readers can then read the diagram at 100% zoom.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save states only for commits in the undo diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The activity diagram of the proposed undo/redo feature saves a new
state for every command that changes patient data. undo and redo
change patient data too, so by the diagram they would purge the redo
states and save a new one.

This contradicts Steps 4 to 6 of the walkthrough, where undo only
moves the pointer.

Let's guard the branch with "command commits patient data", as the
walkthrough describes.

The diagram then matches the steps around it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the undo self-call in UML notation
commitResults.messageBody:
In the Model sequence diagram of the proposed undo feature, the
resetData self-call has no activation bar or return, and its argument
is a type, while every other call names a value.

A self-call is drawn with its own activation bar in the course's UML
notation.

Let's give resetData an activation bar and a dashed return, and pass
it a value, previousState.

The diagram then uses the same notation as the other diagrams.

commitResults.messageTitle: Attach the purged-state note to its state
commitResults.messageBody:
The last state diagram of the undo walkthrough has the note "State s2
deleted." on the arrow from the current-state pointer to s3, so it
reads as a note about the pointer or s3.

The note is meant to say that s3 takes the place of the purged s2.

Let's attach the note to s3, saying that s3 was saved after s2 was
purged, as in Step 6.

The note then names the state it describes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Leave the JDK calls out of the due diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The due sequence diagram shows calls to Clock.systemDefaultZone() and
LocalTime.now(clock). These JDK calls are at a lower level than the
rest of the diagram, and their two lifelines make it about 1340
pixels wide, so the page shrinks it.

The DG text already explains where the clock and the current time
come from.

Let's remove the two JDK lifelines and their calls, and say in the
note that the command gets the current time from its clock.

The diagram is then about as wide as the delete diagram, and shows the
same level of detail.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add result screenshots to due and editmed in UG
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide has screenshots for only help and find. The due and
editmed sections describe their results in text alone, although
both show their result in the main window: due in the result box,
and editmed in the result box and the detail panel.

A screenshot lets a reader check what the result looks like, e.g.,
which doses are marked (earlier today).

Let's add a screenshot of the main window under the due example and
under the first editmed example, taken from the app on the sample
data at 10:30, as the examples are.

Each screenshot then shows exactly the result that its example
describes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use full-window screenshots for due and editmed
commitResults.messageBody:
The due and editmed screenshots in the User Guide are crops of the
main window without its title bar, shown at 740 pixels. The help and
find screenshots show the whole window with the macOS title bar, at
560 pixels.

Screenshots in one guide should look the same, so that readers can
tell at a glance that each one shows the MediConnect window.

Let's replace both with full-window screenshots of the same results,
and show them at 560 pixels, as the find screenshot is.

The result screenshots in the User Guide then share one style.

commitResults.messageBody: Added a note about planned NRIC display for future version.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn only about moved appointments in editappt
commitResults.messageBody:
editappt ends its result with the notes and warnings of addappt, e.g.,
"Note: this appointment is in the past.", after every edit. So editing
only the note of a past appointment, e.g., to record what was said at
the visit, says each time that the appointment is in the past.

The UG gives these notes and warnings only for an appointment moved
into the past, more than 2 years ahead, or to the date and time of
another appointment, so a tester may report the repeated ones as a bug.

Let's give them only when the edit changes the date or time.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say in UC15 only a moved appointment is warned
commitResults.messageBody:
UC15 says that an edited appointment in the past, more than 2 years
ahead, or at the same date and time as another appointment gets the
same note or warning as in UC14. editappt now gives them only when the
edit moves the appointment, so the use case no longer matches it.

Let's say in extension 3a that the edit moves the appointment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update addappt steps and index terms in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG's addappt implementation says that the command rejects only a
duplicate appointment and notes only one in the past. It also rejects
an appointment before the patient's date of birth, and notes one more
than 2 years ahead, so the steps and the sequence diagram are out of
date. The glossary also defines MED_INDEX and APPT_INDEX but not
CONTACT_INDEX, CI_INDEX and ALLERGY_INDEX, which the UG uses.

Let's add the date-of-birth check and the far-ahead note to the steps
and the diagram, and add the three index terms to the glossary.

commitResults.messageTitle: State data file and name rules in the UG
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG invites users to edit the data file, but does not say that
names, phones and addresses there are not tidied as commands tidy
them, so a double space in a name or a hyphen in a phone makes the
file invalid, and an address starting with a space is reported as
blank. It also does not say that names cannot have brackets or commas,
or that backup and restore can move data to another computer. It calls
the folder of the data file by another name than the home folder.

Changing the validation now could break what works, so let's state
these rules in the UG instead, add backup and restore to the FAQ on
moving data, and call the folder the home folder.
